results.body_text: FOR FREELANCERS & SMALL AGENCIES Good work deserves a clearer follow-up. Keep client invoices, due dates and unpaid balances in one place. Know what needs your attention before another week slips by. Start your workspace ↗ See how it works ↓ Invoice tracking in INR. Thoughtful, manual follow-ups. YOUR INVOICE DESK SAMPLE DATA Outstanding ₹42,500 .00 Three invoices. One clear view. SN Studio North INV-014 · Due 12 Oct ₹18,000 Overdue AL Amber Labs INV-015 · Due 30 Oct ₹16,500 Pending FF Field & Form INV-016 · Due 31 Oct ₹8,000 Pending ↗ A little less chasing. A little more clarity. 01   Capture the details 02   See what’s outstanding 03   Follow up with context THE DETAILS, TAKEN CARE OF Your invoice list. With room to breathe. For the admin between finishing a project and confirming a payment. ▤ One place for every record Add a client name, invoice number, amount and due date. Include an email address or notes when they help you keep the context. ◷ A clearer view of what’s due Review outstanding and overdue totals. Filter pending, overdue and paid invoices, or search by client and invoice number. ↗ Follow-ups you control Copy a reminder with the invoice details already filled in. Check the message before sending it through your usual communication tool. ↓ Records you can take with you Edit invoice details, mark confirmed payments and export your current view as a CSV. Each account has its own invoice records. A SIMPLE ROUTINE From “sent” to “settled.” Read the invoice tracking guide ↗ Add the invoice you sent Record the details from your existing invoice document. Use the agreed due date so your tracker reflects the arrangement with your client. Check in on what’s unpaid See which invoices are still pending and which need attention. Confirm the latest payment status before preparing a reminder. Follow up, then update Review and send your reminder yourself. Once you confirm that payment arrived, mark the invoice paid to keep your totals current. A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS Before you open your desk. What is Invoice Desk? Invoice Desk is a tracker for invoices you have already issued. Record the client, invoice number, amount and due date, then use your workspace to review unpaid balances and prepare follow-ups. Does it send reminders automatically? No. Copy a reminder draft from an unpaid invoice, review the wording and send it through your own email or messaging app. You stay in control of every message. Can I create tax invoices or invoice PDFs? The current version tracks invoice records. It does not generate PDFs, calculate GST or other taxes, manage partial payments, or verify bank payments. Keep your original invoice and payment documents separately. Who can see my invoices? Invoices are linked to your account. Other customer accounts cannot access them through the API. Authorized administrators and the hosting operator may access stored data to operate the service. MAKE SPACE FOR THE WORK Keep the next follow-up off the back of your mind. results.body_text: INVOICE DESK GUIDE Polite payment reminder examples A useful payment reminder identifies the invoice, states the due date and asks a clear question. Keep the tone consistent with your client relationship and check the payment record before sending. Before the due date A brief note before the agreed date can help your client spot missing paperwork. Avoid saying the invoice is overdue when the due date has not passed. Give the client a simple way to tell you if they need another copy or a purchase-order reference. Hello [name], a quick reminder that invoice [number] for [amount] is due on [date]. Please let me know if you need another copy or any details to arrange payment. Thank you. After the due date If the due date has passed, first check that payment has not arrived under a different reference. Then send a short note that names the invoice and asks when payment is expected. You do not need to assume why a payment is late. Hello [name], I’m following up on invoice [number] for [amount], which was due on [date]. Could you confirm when payment is expected? If it has already been sent, please share the payment reference so I can update my records. Thank you. A second follow-up For a second reminder, refer to your earlier message and ask whether anything is preventing payment. If the client has already given you an expected date, acknowledge that date instead of sending an unrelated template. Hello [name], I’m checking in on my earlier message about invoice [number]. Could you share an update on payment, or let me know if any information is still needed from me? I’d appreciate an expected payment date so I can keep my records current. Check the details before you send Replace every placeholder with the correct client name, invoice number, amount and date. Confirm the recipient is the person responsible for the invoice. If you attach an invoice copy, check that it matches the number and amount in your message. Read your previous conversation for agreed changes. Remove wording that no longer applies, and do not include extra financial or personal details that the recipient does not need. Keep a record of your message and any reply in the communication tool you normally use. Use a reminder draft in Invoice Desk Open your workspace, find an unpaid invoice and choose Copy reminder. Invoice Desk prepares the message using the saved client name, amount, number and due date. The wording changes depending on whether the due date has passed. Paste the draft into your email or messaging app, review it and send it yourself. Invoice Desk does not automatically send messages or record whether a client has read them. Once you confirm payment in your records, mark the invoice paid so it no longer appears in the unpaid list. Keep your next follow-up in view. results.body_text: INVOICE DESK GUIDE How to track client invoices When you work with several clients, an invoice can be easy to send and easy to forget. A short, consistent tracking routine helps you see what is due and decide which client to contact next. Record each invoice in one place Start with the client name, a unique invoice number, the amount and the agreed due date. Use the same invoice number that appears on the document you sent to your client. Keep a copy of that document in your usual records. Add the invoice to your tracker when you send it. Waiting until a payment is late makes it harder to see the full picture. Optional notes can hold a purchase-order reference or the person handling payment, without putting sensitive account details into a general notes field. Separate pending, overdue and paid Pending means the invoice is unpaid but its due date has not passed. Overdue means the due date has passed and you have not marked payment as received. Paid means you have checked your payment records and confirmed receipt. Invoice Desk calculates pending and overdue status from the due date, using the Asia/Kolkata time zone. An invoice due today stays pending. It becomes overdue the next day if it remains unpaid. Payment status is updated manually; the app does not connect to your bank. Review balances on a regular schedule Choose a repeatable review time, such as the start of your workweek. Look at the outstanding total, then the overdue total. Check older invoices before writing reminders so you do not contact a client who has already paid. For each unpaid invoice, look for a recent reply, an agreed extension or a missing document. A reminder is more useful when it reflects the conversation already in progress. If the agreed due date changes, update the record so the next review uses the correct date. Keep your records consistent Mark an invoice paid only after confirming receipt. If you make a mistake, change it back to unpaid. You can edit a client name, amount or date when correcting the record, and Invoice Desk keeps an activity history of invoice changes. Export a CSV when you need a working copy for your own records. CSV exports include the active search and status filter, so clear those filters first if you want the full list. A filtered export is useful for a follow-up list, but it is not a full database backup. Know what the tracker does Invoice Desk tracks existing invoices in INR. It does not generate invoice PDFs, calculate tax, handle partial payments or verify bank transactions. Keep your original invoice documents and payment records alongside your tracker. Start with a small set of invoices, check the totals against your records, and make the review routine part of closing each client project. You can use the reminder examples in the next guide when you are ready to follow up. Keep your next follow-up in view. Track due dates and prepare a reminder from your saved invoice details.
